summary: Junkei Washio (1868–1941) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Toyo University (~1888–1891). He later held posts at Toyo University, Komazawa University, and Sendan-Rin School.

Junkichi Imanishi (1935–2022) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He taught at Hokkaido University (~1968–1996) and held professorial and directorship roles at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the IIBS.

Junko Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the Australian National University (MA, 1980) and the University of Göttingen (doctoral dissertation, 1990), and was a professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2011).
Junko Minamoto (born 1947) works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Otani University and held a post at Kansai University.

Junsho Kato (born 1939) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at KU Leuven and the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa, Hajime Nakamura, Étienne Lamotte, and Juntaka Kato, later holding professorships at Nishogakusha University and Nagoya University.

Junyi Tang (1909–1978) was a philosopher and sinologist. He studied at Peking University and under Thomé H. Fang and Shili Xiong, and held posts at National Central University (~1940–1949) and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies (~1953–1978).
Junzo Inagaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoshin Fukihara. He held a post as section chief (課長) at Otani University.
Juro Watanabe is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Gerhard Oberhammer and held a post at the University of Tsukuba (attested 1989–1990).
Jushu Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts as a part-time lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 2005) and at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).

Justin McDaniel (born 1972) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2011–2018).

Justin R. Ritzinger is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett, and held posts at Dharma Drum Mountain, Dharma Drum Buddhist College, Academia Sinica, and Oberlin College.
Justin Shimeld is a philosopher. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania (attested 2012), where he studied under doctoral supervisors Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.

Justus Olshausen (1800–1882) was an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar. Educated at Kiel and Berlin, and under Silvestre de Sacy, Langlès, and Kieffer, he held posts at the University of Kiel (~1827–1848) and the University of Königsberg (~1848–1853).

János Szerb (1951–1988) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1972–1980). He held posts at the University of Vienna (1982) and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (~1985–1988).
Jérôme Ducor (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Jacques May (~1980–1993) and held a post at the University of Lausanne (~1995–2019).

Józef Kowalewski (1800–1878) studied at Svislač gymnasium, Vilnius University, and Kazan Imperial University. Specializing in Iranian/Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, he held posts at Kazan Imperial University (~1828–1860, serving as rector in 1855) and the University of Warsaw (~1862–1878).
József Budenz (1836–1892) was a linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey (~1855–1858). He later held a post at Eötvös Loránd University from ~1868 to 1892.

Jörg Heimbel works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tibet University and the University of Hamburg (PhD, 2014) under David P. Jackson, Dorji Wangchuk, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, later serving as a Tibetan lecturer at Hamburg (attested 2019).
Jörg Plassen (born 1968) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He has held professorships at Geumgang University and Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2013).

Jørn Borup (1966–2023) worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Aarhus University (~1999–2002) under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, and served there as Associate Professor from ~2009 to 2023.
